events.title: NCSA Mosaic 1.0 released
events.summary: On January 23, 1993, the National Center for Supercomputing Applications released Mosaic 1.0 — the browser that popularized inline images and made the web mainstream.
events.about: Mosaic showed the web as a visual medium: pictures inside pages, clickable links, and forms on Windows, Mac, and Unix. Marc Andreessen's team at NCSA turned a research network into something ordinary users wanted — and its alumni founded Netscape.

narrative.whyChosen: Mosaic was the tipping point from academic hypertext to mass-market browsing.
narrative.whyImportant: Inline images and a polished UI made the web understandable to non-specialists and sparked the first web boom.
narrative.problemSolved: Earlier browsers were niche research tools; the public needed one friendly program that worked across platforms.
